newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK HIKES MINIMUM CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK HIKES MINIMUM CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Tuesday raised minimum capital requirements for local banks nearly five-fold to adjust for inflation and enforce international prudential standards.

Under a capital adequacy regulation published in the State Gazette banks will be required to have a minimum of 10 billion levs of own capital by June 30, 1998, up from current 2.2 billion levs for a full licence and 1.4 billion levs for a domestic one.
Investors applying for a new banking licence will be required to have paid in at least 10 billion levs capital also by the end of June next year.

The current requirements were introduced by the BNB in 1996 but since the beginning of this year they have become incompatible with prudential regulations because of accumulated inflation and the sharp fall in the lev.
Year-on-year consumer price inflation was 1,527 percent in June.
Under an IMF-prescribed currency board regime introduced on July 1 the lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark as anchor to curb inflation and restore confidence in the banking system.

The new BNB regulation sets equal minimum capital requirements for a full and a domestic licence because banks will have to meet other prudential banking requirements before the BNB decides to grant them a full licence.

"It will not be enough to have 10 billion lev capital to be granted a full licence. Operations abroad will be permitted only when the bank meets other requirements, for example capital to risk assets ratio," a BNB Banking Supervision Department official told Reuters.

Local branches of foreign banks will not be required to have a minimum capital of 10 billion levs when they meet international capital adequacy standards and the foreign bank has the required capital in the country of registration.
An additional requirement for foreign banks' branches is that they place with the BNB a permanent guarantee issued by the foreign bank to cover any liability of the branch.
Foreign banks which have branches in Bulgaria will be required to submit their profit and loss accounts and balance sheets to the BNB at least once a year.
They will be exempt from covering the paid-in capital requirement only with permission from the BNB Supervision Department.
The supervision department might require from the branch to maintain with the BNB a lev- or foreign currency-denominated deposit amounting to five percent of the branch's balance sheet liabilities.

Under the new BNB regulation banks have to boost their own capital-to-risk assets ratio to a minimum of eight percent by the end of this year, to 10 percent by end-1998 and to 12 percent by the end of 1999. -- Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
